quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road is ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. This is dangerous because you won't have time to stop if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on vehicles that travel slowly.

questions.question: When a school bus stops on the road to pick up or drop off children, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has its lights flashing and its stop arm out. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is raised before you go. Also check that no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are usually marked with white lines. They may be marked in different ways, but some crosswalks have no markings at all.

questions.question: You see lowered gates and flashing lights at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates are raised.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates are raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when you see warning signs, lights, or a flagger. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead. Drivers in that lane need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: What is the rule for children under age 16 in a moving vehicle?

options.text: They must be restrained at all times.
They must be restrained only on freeways.
Parents can choose whether to restrain them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must be restrained at all times.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt. Make sure all passengers wear seat belts or child restraints. The law requires all people in a vehicle to be restrained.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and don't need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Always be careful near railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that making a U-turn is not allowed.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on the water like water skis.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Cyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: You see a green traffic light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter the intersection until you can cross it completely.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter the intersection until you can cross it completely.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic signal turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with care.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To avoid the dangers of tired driving, take breaks every hour on long trips. When possible, share driving with another person so you can each rest while the other drives.

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There isn't enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
The crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: There isn't enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time from either direction. Do not stop on the railroad tracks. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet in front of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, move back into your original lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough space to safely pull in front.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and prepare to yield or stop before turning.

questions.question: What does a sign with this shape mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A yellow diamond sign warns of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: To prevent skidding on snow or ice, shift to low gear before going down a steep hill. Leave more space between you and the car ahead. Avoid quick stops. If you don't have antilock brakes, pump the brakes to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving behind another vehicle at night?

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet from the car ahead.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beam when you are following another driver closely.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain at speeds as low as 30 mph, your tires may lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you traffic laws that you must obey. Where this sign is posted, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: How can you avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make abrupt turns.
Apply the brakes firmly.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas, do not brake, keep the vehicle straight, and let it slow down.

questions.question: What should you do if it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road?

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose contact with the road, ease off the gas pedal and avoid the brakes. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Make speed and direction changes slowly and carefully.
Drive as you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make speed and direction changes slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly and carefully. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose contact with the road and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an octagonal sign?

options.text: Slow.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign means Stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.
